newsitem.title: USA: Acme Metals Q4 hurt by steel making unit.
newsitem.headline: Acme Metals Q4 hurt by steel making unit.

text.p: Acme Metals Inc, posting a loss for the fourth quarter compared with a year-ago profit, said its steel making segment reported an operating loss of $11.4 million compared with operating income of $5.1 million last year.
It said its steel fabricating segment had $4.3 million in operating income compared with operating income of $3.9 million in the same 1995 period.

"Our steel making segment was adversely affected by anticipated training and startup costs and inefficient operations related to commissioning the new thin slab caster and hot strip mill complex," said president Stephen Bennett.

The company began to record depreciation and previously capitalized interest expense mid-fourth quarter in connection with the start-up of its new facility for producing minigrated steel, combining highly efficient mini-mill casting and rolling technologies with Acme's traditional liquid steel.
Bennett, in a statement, said the transition to the new facility from existing operations will continue until mid-1997.
Acme reported a fourth-quarter loss of $0.59 a share compared with a year-earlier profit of $0.53. Sales fell to $119.9 million from $131.7 million.
